articles.title: Prologue - Unknown Space Walkthrough - Crimson Desert Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Unknown Space is the second major main quest in Crimson Desert. The second half of the Prologue chapter introduces you to the Abyss and gives you a taste of
articles.body:
Unknown Space is the second major main quest in Crimson Desert . The second half of the Prologue chapter introduces you to the Abyss and gives you a taste of Crimson Desert's style of puzzles. There's no fighting here, but it's easy to get lost in the Corridor of the Void. This IGN guide will help you find your way back to the surface.

Stuck on a specific subquest in the Prologue questline? Click the links to jump straight to our dedicated walkthroughs below:

After losing to Myurdin, you'll find yourself in a strange place called the Corridor of the Void to start the Realm of Uncertainty quest. Up ahead, there's a little parkour section. If you want to take a beat to learn more about the lore of Crimson Desert, you can now pause and get access to far more menus.

If you want to learn more about the Greymanes and other aspects of Crimson Desert you've encountered or "learned" so far, go to "Others" and scroll to the "Knowledge" subsection. Otherwise, it's best to continue forward. Run and jump across the first platform and gap. With the second, it's time to learn something new!

You can try to jump across normally, but some of the pillars are really small. To get around this, you can use Crimson Desert's precision jump mechanic. Hold L1 / LB / Ctrl to aim , then place your cursor on the spot you want to reach. With the button still held, press Square / X / Space to jump to the exact spot you've highlighted.

This isn't a required mechanic to get across, but it's nice to have in your pocket in case you need to do some precision platforming. On the other side of the gap, jump over the wall to climb it. You can climb just about any wall in Crimson Desert as long as you have enough stamina!

Following the path forward, you'll hit a checkpoint and reach another wall to climb. This one is taller, but you still have enough stamina to reach the top. You can also jump while climbing, but that costs way more stamina. Just hold the left stick forward to climb this wall for now.

At the top of the path, there's a small hole in the wall past a waterfall. Do not touch the waterfall unless you want to start from the checkpoint. At the hole, crouch by pressing Left Stick Click or roll by pressing the dodge button to squeeze through it. Kliff can also automatically crouch as you approach the small space.

Through the hole, a set of platforms will create a path to the next area. No parkour required here!

Up ahead, you'll be introduced to the Blinding Flash mechanic. By pressing LB + RB or L1 + R1 , Kliff will angle his sword to reflect light. You can use this to spot points of interest while exploring Pywel, and you can even use it during fights to temporarily blind enemies!

You need to use Concentrating Light to get through the door blocking your path, however. To do so, activate Blinding Flash by holding the two shoulder buttons. While pressing those , lift your finger to press and hold L1 / LB a second time. This will activate Concentrating Light .

You know how a magnifying glass can concentrate sunlight and start a fire? This is basically the same thing. Kliff focuses the light to activate switches in the Abyss or ignite vines and other obstacles. Use Concentrating Light on the switch above the door to reveal the way forward.

Through the door, there's another gap to cross, this time with three moving platforms in water. Wait for them to line up, then hop across. Don't worry about falling into the water. Kliff can swim to the other side if you miss a jump.

The next area is really dark, so it's time to learn about the lantern.

The lantern is an incredibly important tool in Crimson Desert since it highlights important locations and other helpful items just like Blinding Flash.

The lantern is automatically equipped for this tutorial. However, should it get unequipped, you can equip it by bringing up the radial wheel (press D-pad Left ) and using the Right Stick to select the lantern. Press Cross / A to select it and turn it on if it doesn't automatically light itself.

The lantern is attached to Kliff's hip, so it'll automatically illuminate the surrounding area. If you hold L1 / LB to aim, you can focus the light to view the area ahead and highlight any important objects. Focus the lantern's light on the tubes running along the floor, then follow them to reach the exit.

In the next area, step onto the pedestal at the end of the path to leave the Corridor of the Void and return to Pywel after a cutscene featuring Kliff's fallen allies. Your adventure continues on the surface!

Back on the surface, you'll start the New Journey quest. Months have passed since the ambush, and Kliff still mourns his lost Greymane companions.

A man named Sebastian fished Kliff out of the river following the Greymanes' defeat at the hands of the Black Bears. Follow him up the hill to his cabin to continue the quest. You can explore a bit here, but we'd recommend holding off on picking up too much. You can pet the dog by the fisherman, though!

See those fishermen on the riverbank? Observe them with L1 / LB to learn about fishing. You can gain knowledge of enemies, activities, and other useful things by observing people across Pywel, so keep an eye out for anything out of the ordinary! Important people (like these fisherman) will have their names highlighted in gold instead of white.

As you walk up the hill, keep an eye out for a lit brazier on the right next to a stump and a variety of items. Pick up the meat-like item to get your first easy, yet helpful, recovery item. There's a Bekker Axe you can take too and equip if you want something with a slightly higher attack than your current sword.

When you reach the cabin, you'll get a cutscene where Sebastian recommends you visit Hernand Tavern for information. Suddenly, some bandits come knocking. It's just a pair of enemies, so you should be able to make quick work of them.

For your help, Sebastian will reward you with an inventory expansion of three slots, bringing you up to 53.

Inventory space is quite limited in Crimson Desert, and the main way to expand it is by completing side quests and favors for the residents of Pywel. Keep an eye out for inventory upgrades in quest reward lists! Some vendors also sell bags that increase inventory capacity.

That being said, when you collect items early on, don't get too precious about keeping them. It can't hurt to pick things up and sell them to merchants for some quick money. Especially considering all you have are a few arrows and the sword you floated in with!

Before you follow Sebastian up the hill, and especially if you're interested in fishing, take a minute to go back to the river. Cross it on the shallow parts to the small island in the middle where the herons stand in a big flock. If you run in brandishing your weapon, flail it a few times, and you should get a kill.

Walk to any fallen birds and press the prompt to skin them. This awards you a few crafting items, bird meat, and a large bone that sells for a meager but helpful amount. Continue north on the island, past the two trees, into the flower patch near the water.

You can grab a dried fish on a rock, and even better, a free fishing rod. This is before you're given the tutorial side quest to learn fishing, but if you want to get ahead, you can do so here.

When you're satisfied with your exploration of the area, return to Sebastian. He offers to lead you to Hernand , the first major settlement of the game and the hub for most of your activities in the opening hours of your journey. He's even kind enough to give you a horse, so mount up and ride alongside him.

If you look around the field up here before mounting your new steed, you'll find raspberries, all manner of flowers, and some food and tools left behind on various tree stumps and large rocks. Things to sell when you get to town, basically.

If there's something you can't reach in a container, basket, or barrel, hit the wooden item with your weapon to destroy it. You can put away your weapons by tapping D-pad Left or T . When you're ready to go, mount the horse Sebastian has offered you.

This horse is a Herspia , which is a standard steed commonly found across Pywel. There are other horse breeds to tame or purchase, and you can upgrade your mount with new abilities like drifting or double jumping by riding and raising your bond with them.

Once you reach Hernand with Sebastian, the prologue will finally come to a close with a cutscene of Sebastian introducing the outskirts of the town. He takes his leave, and you'll enter Chapter 1 .

You can freely explore Pywel if you wish, but you really should continue with Chapter 1 to unlock some awesome traversal abilities. IGN's Crimson Desert walkthrough continues with Chapter 1's Trials of Kindness .

After Kliff stands, alone and ready to face what's next, you'll get a prompt notifying you that you've been given a temporary place to stay. This location got an important change in Patch 1.00.03. You'll now find a private storage chest in your tent. This chest holds up to 240 items, giving you a place to stash your gear during the early game. It will eventually move to a new location as you progress through the main story, but for now, this is where you should stick anything you want to hang on to.

articles.title: Chapter 1 - Traces Walkthrough - Crimson Desert Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Traces is the second part of Chapter 1 in Crimson Desert. This quest takes you to Hernand Castle and gives you a brand new set of powers that'll make
articles.body:
Traces is the second part of Chapter 1 in Crimson Desert . This quest takes you to Hernand Castle and gives you a brand new set of powers that'll make exploration and combat much easier. This IGN guide will show you where to use the Mystical Key in Hernand Castle and how to master your new Abyss powers.

Need help with a particular quest in the Chapter 1: Traces Questline? Click the links below to jump to:

To start Mystical Key, pick up the strange Engraved Key on the ground after helping Rulupee recover her cat from the roof in the Trials of Kindness quest. Examine the key, and you'll be sent to back to camp for your next objective.

Back at his tent, Kliff takes a closer look at the key and remembers the beggar's words from earlier about the castle having the answers he seeks. Next stop, Hernand Castle!

Before you go to far, climb up the nearby tower and ring the bell at the top. This will clear the fog on your map and reveal the surrounding area! Bells like this can be found all over Pywel, so always check for them in new areas. Some are even hidden! You can find them with ease by checking out the Bell Tower Locations (How to Unfog the Map) guide.

To continue, make your way up to the Hernand Castle gate next to the encampment. You'll get turned away at the gate because of your appearance, so you'll need a fancy new outfit to gain access to the castle's interior .

Since you helped the tailor for the Trials of Kindness quest, you already have one. As a reward for cleaning the tailor's chimney, you'll receive a set of Hernandian Attire . Equip it from the key items (armor) section of your inventory and the guards will have no choice but to let you through the castle's gate.

Continue through the gate and enter the castle. Along the path, you'll pass by the Contribution Shop .

Here, you can spend Contribution to get cool armor and other items. Come back once you've completed more side quests !

Contribution points are limited, but you can always sell items back to the Contribution Shop to get your points back.

Past the Contribution Shop and through the castle's interior gate (after another pair of guards and a clothing inspection), you'll finally enter the castle's main hall. As soon as you enter, turn right and head up the stairs to reach the second floor.

You'll reach an area with another set of wooden stairs, but ignore them for now. Instead, head past the two guards into the hallway on the right.

Past those guards is another hall with wooden doors on both sides and a chandelier hanging from the ceiling. Enter the first door on your left (the one that the maid mentions is always locked) to continue your quest.

Open the glowing treasure chest inside the room to obtain a Faded Abyss Artifact and an Abyss Artifact , which will both come in handy later. Then, step through the glowing gateway by the bookshelves. This will bring you to the Abyss, a series of floating islands in the sky above Pywel.

Polar Opposites sees you entering the Abyss. So, when you're ready, walk forward and step onto the stone pedestal at the beginning of the path in front of you.

This is an Abyss Nexus . It's a fast travel point. These are hidden all across Pywel, and they're very hard to find. Use Blinding Flash to spot potential Abyss Nexus sites from a distance while exploring! After unlocking the Abyss Nexus, head toward the tower at the end of the path. A white bird will then fly down and grant you a new power: Axiom Force .

Have you played The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom? Axiom Force is basically Ultrahand. You can move stuff around and solve puzzles with it, and it even has some combat capabilities once you've unlocked some upgrades.

To use Axiom Force, press and hold Left Stick Click . This will shoot out a grabby hand wherever you're aiming. To the right of the tower, you'll see some tubes running through the grass. There are two stone plates connecting the tubes, but they're out of alignment. Use Blinding Flash or your lantern to see the power lines running through the tubes and the stone plates.

To fix them, use Axiom Force to rotate the circular stone plates.

Once you've rotated the plates so the blue lines are connected to the tubes, the tower's door will open. Head inside to meet a familiar face and learn more about the impending threat looming over Pywel.

Your next task that pops up is Abyss Without Balance . After talking to the weird wizard in the tower, it's time for some more puzzle-solving. You need to fix a skybridge to continue.

Walk through the triangular gate ahead of you to get started. Then, use Axiom Force to grab the circular switch embedded in the pedestal in front of you. You have to grab that specific spot or this won't work!

Once you've grabbed hold of the switch, use the D-Pad to slowly rotate it. You're looking for a sweet spot here. Rotate until you feel a vibration and see glowing blue energy. That's how you know you've got the right angle.

Hold the switch in the right spot to align it and activate the next part of the skybridge. Then, jump across the floating platforms to reach the next area.

Climb all the way to the grassy area, and you'll reach a chasm that's way too wide to cross on your own. Thankfully, there are some moving platforms that'll carry you even higher. Wait for one to get close enough, then hop on and enjoy the ride.

Once you reach your destination, step onto the pedestal on the ground to warp to the next part of the skybridge.

Do a little bit more parkour until you reach another Abyss Nexus. Stand on the pedestal to activate it and unlock a fast travel point. Time for another puzzle.

To solve this next puzzle, you need to move the floating power core to the deactivated lantern. If you try to drop down into the lowered area, you'll be stopped by an invisible floor.

Axiom Force is the solution here. Use the hand to grab the blue electric cube floating in the air above everything else.

Then, drag it onto the stone pedestal on the side of the pit. There's another lantern nearby that you can see as a reference.

Once you've moved the power core to the right spot, the floor will no longer be blocked. Drop down for the next part of the puzzle.

Now, you need to combine the Abyss Cell. It's going to take a little bit of elbow grease. First, use Axiom Force to grab the floating electric brick. Then, carry it to the highlighted spot on the wall where all the tubes connect to.

You'll see a hologram of a person repeating the same animation. Hold L1 / LB to observe and learn a new skill: Force Palm .

Force Palm is a concentrated energy blast activated by pressing Right Stick Click . It can be used to solve puzzles, break objects, or stun enemies during combat. For now, use it to smack the Abyss Cell into its slot on the wall. When it's in the right spot, it'll be highlighted in green.

Once everything is hooked up and plugged in, you need to activate the Abyss power supply as the final step of the process. The power supply is the giant wheel on the wall. The camera pans over to show it to you after you slam the Abyss Cell into place.

Climb up onto the wheel, hang onto the middle of it, then press Right Stick Click to unleash Force Palm while you're still clinging to the wheel. Think of the middle like a giant power button. Give it a good smack, and you'll get everything back online.

Afterward, climb the stairs and claim the Abyss Artifact waiting for you at the pedestal up top. Abyss Artifacts are Crimson Desert's skill points . Thankfully, these can't be sold, so you don't have to worry about accidentally parting with one.

Using an Abyss Artifact will get you Abyss Links — essentially duplicate skill points — for Crimson Desert's other playable characters once they're unlocked.

Because of this, there's no need to stockpile Abyss Artifacts to level the others up later on. Feel free to upgrade Kliff as soon as you get Abyss Artifacts!

After solving these sky puzzles, you'll be visited by a mysterious woman in white. White Crow the Witch will bestow one final power upon you.

Kliff will then jump off the sky island, giving you the perfect opportunity to test out your new gliding ability. By pressing the jump button midair, you can deploy a set of wings to slow your descent and reach new areas.

Gliding takes quite a bit of stamina, and you can unlock new upgrades like a speed boost or aerial dodge with enough Abyss Artifacts. You'll recover stamina while falling, too, so you can deploy your wings multiple times midair.

Now that you have all of Kliff's basic abilities, you can take a break from the main story and explore. If you need some direction, try some of these activities:

It's also a great idea to buy a pickaxe and start scanning the cliffs for Iron Ore and Copper Ore , two crucial upgrade materials that'll strengthen your weapons and armor. You'll recognize their veins by their dark gray or light blue hues, respectively.

Fall back down to Hernand to complete this quest and move on to the Chapter 2: Golden Greed quest, Unexpected Gift . Traces

articles.title: Spooky Celebration Event Guide - Hello Kitty Island Adventure Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Spooky Celebration is an Annual Event that begins on September 24 and will continue through fall as the primary event for Hello Kitty Island Adventure.
articles.body:
Spooky Celebration is an Annual Event that begins on September 24 and will continue through fall as the primary event for Hello Kitty Island Adventure . It’s Kuromi’s month to shine, and she is going all out by creating one mischievous season to remember! Drink a Kuromi Kool Potion and gear up in Spooky costumes while checking in for Daily Rewards and participating in Kuromi’s Spooky Celebration for even more exclusive outfits, furniture, and more!

Drop by Friendship Island every day to earn exclusive Spooky Celebration outfits and accessories alongside Seaside Resort resources through Daily Rewards. You can either check in with My Melody at the Seaside Resort plaza or check the Daily Rewards tab in your game menu.

For the Month of Mischief, Spooky Celebration's Daily Rewards will be broken down into four whopping parts, with Part I through III lasting a total of 14 days. Part I will begin on the same day as the event debuts, and each part after will start a week and two weeks after Spooky Celebration has started. The Finale will begin approximately four weeks after Spooky Celebration has started and will last 12 days.

In addition to Spooky Celebration's Daily Rewards, Kuromi will also be handing out Month of Mischief Potions! Log in to receive all kinds of Potions through Daily Rewards in a separate banner. These potions include Kuromi Kool Potions, Item Potions, Sparkle Potions, Moon Gravity Potions, and Critter Potions. You can also receive some of these potions by picking up items and catching Critters around Friendship Island.

Although Kuromi has taken over for her Month of Mischief, Spooky Celebration can still be celebrated by going around at night and requesting Spooky Treats from your Hello Kitty friends. To obtain the Event Currency, Spooky Treats, you’ll need to don a costume or an item of clothing that has the Spooky tag before venturing out in the guise of night to speak to three residents on Seaside Resort. By selecting the dialogue option “Trick or Treat!”, you’ll be able to obtain 3x Spooky Treats per resident . You can even chat up Island Visitors who will also reward you with Event Currency by crying, “Trick or Treat!”

Complete Daily Quests to obtain additional Spooky Treats, with 1x Spooky Treat per quest . If you have the Wheatflour Wonderland DLC or City Town DLC, you can obtain an extra Spooky Treat, thanks to the additional Daily Quest. By completing all the Daily Tasks and Trick-or-Treating, you can obtain around 4~5 additional Spooky Treats for a total of 13~14 Spooky Treats daily.

Spooky Treats are Spooky Celebration’s Event currency and can be traded in at the Event Stall that is located just outside the Seaside Resort Plaza. Converse with the Master of Festivities, the Nul, situated at the Stall, in order to exchange your Spooky Treats for exclusive Kuromi outfits and furniture, as well as all previous Spooky Celebration outfits and furniture from past events.

Kuromi's Potions, Effects, and How to Gather

During Kuromi’s Month of Mischief, you may find that picking up items may grant you an additional gift as well. While Spooky Celebration is active, you’ll occasionally find Sparkle Potions, Critter Potions, Item Potions, and Moon Gravity Potions! While these won’t have any permanent recipes at Kuromi’s Cauldron, you can gather plenty during your regular collection around the island and have fun with the effects they bring.

For Spooky Celebration, Kuromi has taken over Hello Kitty’s Cafe and has come out with a new collection of Potions for both you and all of her friends on Friendship Island. One of the best potions she has concocted is none other than the Kuromi Kool potion, which she gives to her friends to transform their outfits into Kool and Spooky costumes that are perfect for the season!

Each day, you’ll be tasked with giving Kuromi Kool Potions to two of the residents on Friendship Island. These will be counted as Daily Quests, and you’ll unlock the Hello Kitty characters' Spooky outfits after gifting them their potions.

New Kuromi Recipes for All Cooking Stations

During October, in celebration of Kuromi's Month of Mischief, you'll be able to occasionally find Kuromi Decorating Kits when picking up select items in Spooky Swamp. These Decorating Kits can be used to craft not only Kuromi's Birthday Cake, but also many new recipes across all Cooking Stations in Hello Kitty Island Adventure! Head to the Spooky Swamp to pick up Swampmallows , Glow Berries , Spinip , and Pumpkins for a chance to pick up a Kuromi Decorating Kit! Below are all of the new Kuromi Decorating Kit Recipes you can make:

articles.title: Days of Plenty Event Guide - Hello Kitty Island Adventure Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Days of Plenty is an Annual Event that begins on October 8 and will continue to run through October as the secondary event in Hello Kitty Island Adventure
articles.body:
Days of Plenty is an Annual Event that begins on October 8 and will continue to run through October as the secondary event in Hello Kitty Island Adventure until October 30. Share your gratitude amongst your friends and celebrate the fall season as the tree leaves change from green to orange. Running through leaf piles may just reward you with some valuable items!

By visiting Friendship Island every day, you will be rewarded with Daily Rewards from My Melody or by checking the Daily Rewards tab in your Game Menu. These rewards range from exclusive clothing and accessories for Days of Plenty to materials that you can use to craft up recipes for new furniture that My Melody has crafted for the season!

Daily Rewards will be broken down into parts, with Part I lasting 10 days and beginning at the same time as the Days of Plenty Event. Part II will start a week after the event has begun and also last for 10 days.

During Days of Plenty, you’ll find Piles of Leaves scattered around Seaside Resort. By running through these piles, you’ll pick up 3x Leaves . Leaves are the Days of Plenty Event Currency, and by exchanging this currency at the Crafting Station Event Stand south of the Seaside Resort plaza, you can obtain exclusive event furniture and clothing. You’ll also be able to find past furniture and outfits at the Event Stand for a discount!

Leaf Piles can be found all around Seaside Resort, spawning in a total of 7 Leaf Piles per day . Running through the piles will reward you with 3 Leaves per pile, netting you 21x Leaves per day to be exchanged at the Crafting Station Event Stand. Since Days of Plenty is a secondary event, completing Daily Missions will not reward you with Leaves.

All Leaf Pile Locations on Seaside Resort

Below is a map of where you can find all of the Leaf Piles in Seaside Resort!

My Melody has been hard at work already crafting up an entirely new furniture set for Days of Plenty, and nothing showcases that better than a new outfit sporting her crafting nature. Tuxedosam is over the moon for an event that’s all about textiles! Participate in Days of Plenty cutscenes and events to unlock all of the new outfits for the Hello Kitty characters.

You can do so by talking to My Melody upon logging in, where she’ll prompt you to participate in the Event. If you want to check back in later, you’ll need to talk to the Master of Festivities, the Event Stand Nul, who is usually located outside the Seaside Resort plaza whenever there’s a new cutscene prompt.

articles.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Season 1 Adds 6 New Maps, New Weapons, and a New DMZ Area
articles.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's Season 1 details have been revealed, and a ton of new content is coming to the game.
articles.body:
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's Season 1 details have been revealed, and a ton of new content is coming to the game.

Activision has confirmed that players can expect six new maps, including the return of Shoot House, in addition to new weapons, modes, events, and an expansion to the game's extraction mode, DMZ. Following the release of Shipment this week , Season 1 will debut with three maps starting on November 6. The maps will vary in weather, with one known as Backstab being set in a snowy village while another one known as Canyon will be set in a toasty desert. Shoot House has been reimagined to fit the game's Korean setting, but the overall layout that fans expect has remained intact.

The map was introduced back in Modern Warfare (2019) and has remained a fan favorite since its introduction for its tight design and powerful sightlines. Three other maps will be added throughout the season as well. Season 1 will also introduce a variety of new weapons, including a tomahawk and weapons that are clearly inspired by the FMG9 and AA-12 from old-school Modern Warfare titles. A gun known as the Cronen Osprey also appears to take inspiration from the CX9 from Modern Warfare (2019) or the Scorpion Evo from Black Ops 2.

All Guns and Weapons in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4

There will also be new attachments/apex attachments to evolve your weapons, including a burst attachment for the M4, which will transform it into an M16. For DMZ enjoyers, a whole new part of the map has been unlocked, known as X01. It's an eerie enclosed facility that players will be able to explore in great detail in favor of finding high-quality loot, but the trade-off is that great threats lie inside. Activision describes the location as a dimly lit "labyrinth" of tunnels and passageways, so don't be surprised if you get lost or disoriented... just make sure you can get out in time for an extraction. You can also expect new bosses, FOB upgrades, and loot.

A number of classic Call of Duty modes such as Infection, Grind, and Drop Zone are also returning in Season 1. And of course, there will be a battle pass with a plethora of skins and unlocks for players. Currently, it looks like there's nothing too outlandish, so don't expect any Nicki Minaj or Beavis and Butthead skins. It seems like Modern Warfare 4 will retain its grounded aesthetic, at least within Season 1. The team had previously promised to avoid over-the-top skins , and so far they're making good on that promise.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: Viture Phantom Beast XR Glasses Are Available for Preorder
articles.body:
The action RPG Phantom Blade Zero is out October 29 (we gave it a 9/10 in our review ). Releasing alongside it are the new Viture Phantom Beast XR Glasses, available for $599 at Viture and IGN Store . This new edition of Viture’s flagship virtual display glasses adds a Phantom Blade Zero theme and it comes with a handful of exclusive accessories. Let’s take a look.

Preorder Viture Phantom Beast XR Glasses

The glasses offer all the same features as standard Viture Beast XR glasses, but with Phantom Blade Zero styling all over the place. The glasses themselves feature black and red imagery inspired by the game. They come with an intricate removable strap, and a scabbard-style case, among other items. Preorders are live now, and if you buy before November 5, you’ll also receive a limited collector’s edition game map.

3 Exclusive Phantom Blade Zero Collectibles: Mó Sanguine Blade Replica Lens Cloth Sticker Set

If you’re not familiar with Viture’s Beast XR Glasses, here’s how they work. First, you connect them to a device like a game console, phone, PC, or handheld gaming device . Then you put them on, and you’ll see a massive virtual display in front of you that effectively looks like a 174-inch screen. You can use this virtual display to play games, watch movies, or do work. And because the glasses are portable, you can use them pretty much anywhere becuase you don't have to lug a huge display with you.

They’re compatible with all sorts of devices, including all the major game consoles (PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and Switch 1/2), plus Windows, MacOS, iOS, Android, and SteamOS. Note that, to connect some of those devices, you’ll need an accessory that’s sold separately. Here’s a rundown of what devices are compatible out of the box, and what accessories are needed for others.

Plug and Play : Windows, MacOS, iOS, Android, Steam Deck, Pro Neckband

With Pro Mobile Dock : Switch 1/2, PS5, PS4, Xbox Series X|S, Xbox One

As for the game, Phantom Blade Zero has already sold an estimated 1 million copies , so it’s going to be a hit right out of the gate. And if you want to be one of them you can check out the global release times and preload details .

Chris Reed is a senior commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's LEGO coverage and maintains the upcoming release dates articles for video games , LEGO sets , and 4K Blu-rays . You can follow him on Bluesky .

articles.title: Apple Announces Its First Touchscreen MacBook
articles.summary: The MacBook Pro has had pretty much the same design since 2021, but today at its 'Pro and Tell' event in Cupertino, Apple has announced an all-new MacBook Pro with a touchscreen.
articles.body:
The MacBook Pro has had pretty much the same design since 2021, but today at its 'Pro and Tell' event in Cupertino, Apple has announced an all-new MacBook Pro with a touchscreen.

The new 'MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display' comes in either a 14- or 16-inch design, just like any other MacBook Pro, just with a Tandem OLED touch display with up to 128GB of RAM. But while the regular MacBook Pro 14 was updated with the M6 chip yesterday, this new touchscreen MacBook Pro will be equipped with either the M5 Pro or M5 Max, both of which will still be more powerful than Apple's new mainstream SoC.

The display is the real star of the show, though, and it should be absolutely gorgeous, coming in with up to 2,000 nits of brightness and a color gamut that covers both the P3 and Adobe RGB spectrums. Couple that with the powerful chips, and this will likely be the laptop to beat for creative professionals who are comfortable on macOS.

Apple MacBook Pro With PROLED XDR Display – Photos

Touchscreen laptops have been around for a while, with Microsoft famously pushing for wide adoption of touch displays with Windows 8. At the time, though, Steve Jobs took a stand against touch displays, even claiming wholeheartedly that 'Touchscreen laptops don't work' back in 2010 . But even though Apple's dad wasn't a fan of touchscreens on laptops, this isn't the first time that Apple has had a touch display on a MacBook, at least if you count the controversial touch bar on the MacBook Pro in the late 2010s.

However, it's clear that the RAM crisis has hit Apple as well. The new Touchscreen MacBook Pro costs an eye-watering $2,899 just to get in the door, which will get you the M5 Pro with a 15-core CPU and a 16-core GPU, along with 24GB of RAM and a 1TB SSD. The 16-inch model is even more expensive, and will set you back $3,399 to start, with a slightly more powerful M5 Pro configuration, along with the same 24GB RAM and 1TB SSD.

Of course, because it's a MacBook, you can absolutely max this thing out if you have the budget for it. Apple will let you spec the 16-inch model with an M5 Max, with an 18-core CPU and 40-core GPU, along with 128GB of RAM and a 16TB SSD for $14,399. Though, that kind of configuration would be absolutely overkill unless you're editing 4K footage every day, and constantly leave your external drive at home.

If you want to get your hands on the new MacBook Pro With PROLED XDR Display, you can preorder it today, and it will show up on store shelves on November 6.

Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

articles.title: How Absolute Batman #25 Changes Everything for Bruce Wayne
articles.summary: Absolute Batman #25 closes out the series' latest storyline with a shocking twist that changes everything for Bruce Wayne. Here's what you need to know.
articles.body:
Full spoilers follow for Absolute Batman #25!

Absolute Batman #25 may well be the most important chapter of this series to date. It marks the end of the "Straw Man" story arc, culminating in the long-awaited showdown between Batman and the Joker and a truly game-changing final page. This issue is such a big deal that the series is going on a short hiatus for the remainder of 2026, leaving readers to sit with these major revelations for a few months.

What happens in issue #25, and how does this showdown redefine Batman's crusade going forward? Here's what you need to know.

DC's Absolute Universe: Preview Art Gallery

Having finally overcome Scarecrow and his relentless campaign of psychological manipulation, this storyline ends with Batman finally venturing into Grimm Manor and preparing to confront the man they call the Joker. There, he's surprised to find not Jack Grimm, but his friends gathered in a sitting room. Waylan Jones, Eddie Nygma, Oswald Cobblepot, and Harvey Dent have all staged an intervention to convince Bruce to give up his fanatical crusade.

In turn, each man admits that they were approached by Jack Grimm, who revealed that he's been secretly helping Bruce evade the authorities. Grimm provided each with evidence that his business empire is 100% legitimate, that he's been campaigning against the Ark-M facility, and that he genuinely wants to help Bruce before Bruce gets himself killed. The friends tell Bruce that he has one last chance to turn himself in for psychological treatment, or else Grimm will finally leak his identity to the authorities.

Batman knows his friends have been fooled by a master manipulator, so he leaps out a window and flees into the woods with the GCPD hot on his trail. He then falls through a hole and lands in Grimm's version of the Batcave, complete with all the trophies that, in another universe, are the rightful property of Bruce himself.

Grimm is waiting for Batman in his disgusting but rejuvenating cocoon of dead babies. He emerges and tells Batman how happy he is to finally have a worthy nemesis again after so many years of boredom. It's here we learn that all the costumes on display in the "Joker Cave" are those worn by warriors that Grimm bested over the years. Previously, the series suggested his origins date back to the 1800s, but it would seem he's actually far older still, possibly dating back to the Roman Empire.

Joker reveals his true, monstrous form and the two men begin battling. Though Batman is able to repeatedly wound Joker with his battle ax and razor-sharp ear daggers, the villain shrugs off the damage and keeps laughing. To him, the funniest joke of all is the idea that one man thinks he can stand up to the systems of power that have existed since the dawn of civilization.

Just as Joker prepares to devour Batman and cut their rivalry short, The Bat (or Barbara Gordon) shows up to give the villain a faceful of her shotgun. The two heroes plunge into the river at the depths of the Joker Cave and make their escape.

The Bat brings Batman back to Harley Quinn's hideout, where they stitch up the battered hero and Batman makes peace with his jilted partner. Batman has survived his first battle with Joker, but it's become clear just how badly outmatched he is. And now he faces the possibility that Joker will escalate their feud by revealing his identity to the world (not that this hulking, 6' 9" powerhouse has ever done a particularly great job of hiding it).

But even that problem takes a backseat to the stunning revelation that closes out issue #25. Bruce is suddenly reunited with Selina Kyle, who reveals she's pregnant. It seems Absolute Batman is about to become a father.

One of the biggest differences between the regular and Absolute versions of Batman is that the latter has more to lose in his quest to save Gotham City. Absolute Batman still has a mother and a loving relationship with Selina. And now that difference looks to be intensified, as he's about to have a child to protect on top of everything else.

The idea of Batman and Catwoman becoming parents is hardly new for DC. In the classic Earth-2 universe, the two eventually marry and raise a daughter named Helena, who grows up to become the vigilante Huntress. At one point it appeared as though DC would follow suit in its core comic book universe with Tom King's Batman series, but they've since rendered the Batman/Catwoman comic that closes out King's run as non-canon.

As you'd expect, this twist is going to dramatically affect the arc of Absolute Batman's journey. Writer Scott Snyder posted on Bluesky , "It'll set the stage for the entire series going forward." More than ever, he stands to lose everything if he doesn't find a way to overcome Jack Grimm and his army of horrible creations.

Let us know what you think of this latest Absolute Batman twist in the comments below. For more on the series, check out IGN's review of Absolute Batman #24 and see how the series reinvented one of Bruce Wayne's greatest tragedies .

Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. Allow him to lend a machete to your intellectual thicket by following @jschedeen on BlueSky .

articles.title: Alien: Isolation 2 Team Confirms Physical Edition, Photo Mode, and New Gameplay Details
articles.summary: The team behind Alien: Isolation 2 released a Q&A that reveals new gameplay details, including using your real-life microphone, a physical edition, a photo mode, and more.
articles.body:
The team behind Alien: Isolation 2 released a Q&A that reveals new gameplay details, including using your real-life microphone, a physical edition, a photo mode, and more.

The team at Creative Assembly released a 17-minute video outlining its vision for Alien: Isolation 2 by answering fan questions about the game, and there's a lot to look forward to. For starters, players can expect a physical edition of the game when it launches in 2027. That means it will beat the deadline to be published on a disc, just ahead of PlayStation's all-digital shift in 2028. The game will also boast a photo mode, which aims to be "everything you expect from a camera."

They're working hard to feature all of the detailed settings you'd expect from an actual camera, such as depth of field, lighting options, filters that call back to the original films, and more. As for the team building this game, about a third of the original crew that made the first title are working on the sequel, but they were looking for big fans when interviewing staff for the initial game. Lead game designer James Green called the sequel a "dream project."

Alien: Isolation 2 will be set months after the first game and, as revealed in a trailer , it will take place partially outside, which will allow the Xenomorph to behave differently. It will use the wider environment to hunt you more effectively by taking advantage of the rough weather and lack of claustrophobic environments where you can typically hear or see it coming. The team is once again trying to tap into the feeling of the original film, where a singular Xenomorph is hunting you as opposed to a whole army of them.

One big feature the team is also pushing is that you can enable an option to toggle your microphone on and off. This will take whatever audio is being fed into your mic, whether it be you screaming, setting down a cup on your desk, or your dog barking, and feed it back into the game. As a result, whatever noise you make in real life could theoretically attract the Xenomorph or other threats.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: Winnie-the-Pooh: Blood and Honey 3 Exclusive Trailer
articles.summary: IGN can exclusively reveal the first trailer for Winnie-the-Pooh: Blood and Honey 3, which director Scott Chambers calls “absolute carnage.” The slasher sequel will open in late January 2027.
articles.body:
IGN can exclusively reveal the first trailer for Winnie-the-Pooh: Blood and Honey 3 , which director Scott Chambers calls “absolute carnage.” You can watch the new trailer via the player above or the embed below. The film’s teaser poster can also be seen below.

“After the brutal capture of Pooh, Tigger, and Rabbit by the sinister Woozles Circus, fifteen years pass and the once-feral creatures are transformed into attractions in a twisted traveling carnival run by the mysterious Karna, occult showman Shandor, and the immortal ringmaster Balthazar. Meanwhile, Momo Milne, an orphan desperate to uncover the truth about her missing mother, traces her last known whereabouts to Woozles Ltd. Alongside her outspoken best friend Billie, Momo infiltrates the circus by taking a job among its bizarre performers,” according to the official synopsis.

“As the girls uncover horrifying secrets behind the spectacle—including drugged half-human creatures, disappearances, and gruesome killings hidden behind the carnival lights—Momo realizes her mother’s disappearance is tied to the circus’ darkest mystery. Drawn into a nightmare where fairy tales become blood-soaked reality, Momo must survive Pooh and his monstrous companions while uncovering the truth before she becomes the next act in Woozles’ deadly show.”

The film is scripted by Richard Stanley (Color Out of Space, Dust Devil, Hardware).

In a statement provided to IGN, director Scott Chambers says “Winnie-the-Pooh: Blood and Honey 3 is absolute carnage. I counted 20 character deaths during filming, and every one of them was captured practically on camera using real prosthetics, special-effects makeup and physical gore effects. I think this is a thrilling new entry in the Blood and Honey universe. It is bigger, bloodier and more ambitious, but it also plays an important part in the wider story we are building. This film leads directly towards Poohniverse: Monsters Assemble—our Avengers-style crossover—and acts as a major stepping stone towards that eventual finale.”

Chambers continued, “The story reveals how these creatures became so angry, damaged and vengeful, giving audiences a deeper understanding of the monsters they have become. It also brings an exciting new character to life in Rabbit, voiced by the legendary Roger L. Jackson from Scream. His performance gives Rabbit a genuinely chilling presence, and I cannot wait for audiences to meet him.”

In addition to Jackson, Chambers and Stanley are also in the cast, with Stanley playing Balthazar Von Woozle. The cast also includes Josephine Blazier, Kira Reed, Leo Harris, Zena Donnelly, and Harrison Davis.

Furthermore, Winnie-the-Pooh: Blood and Honey 3 features prominent social media horror content creators Cris Parker (3C Films) and Slashertalk.

The film is from Jagged Edge Productions and will be distributed by ITN Distribution in late January 2027. Stuart Alson, Nicole Holland, and Evgeny Lensky serve as Executive Producers.

Jim Vejvoda (he/him) is IGN's Assoc. Director of Entertainment Content.

articles.title: Sacha Baron Cohen’s Attempt to Resurrect Ali G Has Gone Disastrously Off the Rails
articles.summary: Sacha Baron Cohen’s attempt to resurrect Ali G goes disastrously off the rails, with barely a joke to be found.
articles.body:
Ali G: Who Iz I? is on Prime Video now, and maybe in a theater near you, though probably not for much longer.

Once the genesis of Sacha Baron Cohen’s mockumentary career, white Rude Boy poseur Ali G now marks its whimper of an ending. Released on Prime Video just five days after its theatrical release, the actor’s directorial debut Ali G: Who Iz I? barely holds together as either cinema or practical joke — let alone where the two have met in the past, by way of his exceptionally enduring Borat. His efforts this time feel especially feeble, landing somewhere in the realm of an unfocused Matt Walsh documentary, where the result isn’t so much laughter, or even provocation, but puzzled annoyance. Fifteen minutes in, one of his unsuspecting targets sums it up succinctly when shown a presentation meant to offend her: “I don’t care.”

Cohen’s latest borrows characters from both HBO’s Da Ali G show as well as his Showtime series Who Is America? in an attempt to weave a political portrait of the modern United States, all wrapped in a flimsy narrative. Like the riotous Borat sequel Subsequent Moviefilm , Who Iz I? is nominally about the wannabe British Rastafari facing fatherhood, when he learns that his longtime girlfriend Julie (Morgana Robinson, taking over for Kellie Bright from the narrative comedy Ali G Indahouse) is pregnant with their child. An attempt to get a third season of his HBO interview series off the ground finds him flying across the pond to LA, where his arrival catches the attention of another Cohen character, Showtime’s Dr. Nira Cain-N'Degeocello, an outdated send-up of liberal academia who hopes to nail him for “cultural appropriation,” despite speaking over people himself.

Along the way, both characters interact with various bystanders in Cohen’s signature prankish style, but his instigations prove limp. There just doesn’t seem to be enough footage to string together a film of everyday subjects responding with outrage, indignation, or even the strained politeness underlying the original Borat from 2006. Two decades later, everyone seems bored by this commonplace, microcelebrity tomfoolery, whether or not they recognize the man behind the makeup. They mostly don’t, though at least one of them, involved in the movie’s confoundingly scattered climax, appears to have gone along with it for the daily rate. Perhaps this is why Cohen feels the need for heavy-handed explanations, in the movie’s opening and closing, of how his mockumentary format works.

The caricatures Cohen portrays feel tame in comparison to a world increasingly divided by political fissures, though given how much the movie’s first half is concerned with “cancel culture” and “DEI” — things even the U.S. government uses as phantom boogeyman — the movie’s mission statement is too askew to root for in the first place. While it does eventually set its sights on those in power, it opts for low-hanging fruit in the form of penile humor that its subjects mostly ignore, forcing Cohen to cut awkwardly around non-reactions.

However, setting aside the movie’s asymmetrical political bent doesn’t yield much of interest to begin with, because Who Iz I? is really only about America on the surface. What it’s really about is Cohen, or rather Ali G, in a way that threatens to be interesting for the briefest moment. Will the character wrestle with his own irrelevance when he fails to secure airtime? Not so fast! Instead, the hamstrung plot grows increasingly obsessed with Dr. Nira’s attempts to find dirt on Ali on make him persona non grata, as though wayward online criticisms of Cohen’s shtick had gotten under his skin and he were trying to pre-empt objections to the movie through Cohen-on-Cohen discourse. If anyone was trying to silence Cohen’s comedy, they’ve clearly been unsuccessful, since he managed to make this movie — though its failures are a product of its own inability to strike while the iron is hot. A three second Cameo from Rachel Dolezal isn’t going to cut it in 2026.

This is largely in line with the film’s M.O. Few gags or targets stick around long enough to let the absurdities land. The Ali G character isn’t so much deployed to prod at people’s politics as he is to be a clownish presence waving his arms for attention, while Cohen also portrays an exaggerated mishmash of what he pictures his critics are like, or what they believe. At the very least, this yields a revealing portrait of artistic insecurity, if an unintentional one. Who Iz I? is a film that takes no risks and has nothing to say, all in service of misguided self-preservation, as Cohen fails to read the tea leaves of a culture that has, for better or worse, long left him behind.

articles.title: Outlander's Sam Heughan Hints at Role in Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum
articles.summary: During a recent appearance at a book festival, Outlander star Sam Heughan strongly suggested that he may have a role in the upcoming film The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum.
articles.body:
Outlander star Sam Heughan has strongly suggested that he may have a role in the upcoming film The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum .

Heughan spoke earlier this month at Scotland’s Wigtown Book Festival, during which the topic of J. R. R. Tolkien’s literary saga and subsequent film adaptations came up.

This wouldn’t be an unusual topic to raise with Heughan, as he’s named after Samwise Gamgee and his brother, Cirdan, is named after an Elf. (Their parents belonged to a London hippie community called Gandalf's Garden.)

When the moderator suggested the Lord of the Rings film franchise was “exhausted” at this point, Heughan cryptically replied, "No, it's not exhausted. I'm not giving anything away, but I may have been in New Zealand recently." You can watch the exchange for yourself below.

Sam Heughan on The Hunt for Gollum — The Mellon Heads - LOTR Podcast (@mellon_heads) October 28, 2026

The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum has been filming in New Zealand under the direction of Andy Serkis .

And as Winter Is Coming points out, “another eagle-eyed Outlander fan account, @samjamie_stillhere, noticed that a rare edition of The Letters of J.R.R. Tolkien went up for auction to benefit the ALS Network, which was signed by ‘people who have taken his world to the screen, and people who are taking it there next.’ The list of signatures includes a number of stars and producers from The Hunt for Gollum, all of whom have their roles for the film listed... as well as Sam Heughan.”

Maybe Heughan was just visiting the set of The Hunt for Gollum as a fan, or perhaps he has a heretofore undisclosed role in the film. If so, who do you think he plays? Let us know in the comments.

For more coverage on all things Middle-earth, read why Jamie Dornan isn’t trying to “outdo” Viggo Mortensen's Aragorn in The Hunt for Gollum and discover why The Rings of Power Season 3 is “turning the page on the show .”

Jim Vejvoda (he/him) is IGN's Assoc. Director of Entertainment Content.
